title: KoreLumina — Builder Core - Commit Guardrail Enforcement — message 1

metadata.content:
This guardrail is correct. What you just hit in the terminal is exactly the problem it’s meant to prevent.
What actually happened (no fluff)


You committed directly on main → blocked by protected branch


You rebased → created conflicts across core builder files


You almost corrupted stable builder state (draft, preview, next.config, etc.)


You had to recover by forcing a branch + manual conflict resolution


That’s exactly the failure mode this guardrail fixes.

FINAL VERSION (USE THIS — SLIGHTLY HARDENED)
Add one missing piece: enforce your kpush script + block dirty state.
KORELUMINA COMMIT GUARDRAIL (ENFORCED)

SCOPE
- One module only
- No cross-module edits

PRE-COMMIT CHECK (ALL YES REQUIRED)
- build passes → yes
- preview renders → yes
- editor visible → yes
- filetree populated → yes
- save overwrites (no append) → yes
- diff visible → yes (if applicable)
- apply works → yes (if applicable)
- no console/runtime errors → yes

IF ANY “NO” → STOP

BRANCH RULES
- NEVER commit on main
- ALWAYS:

  git checkout main
  git pull origin main
  git checkout -b feature/<module>-<task>

COMMIT (ONLY VIA KPUSH)
- DO NOT use raw git push
- ALWAYS use:

  kpush "type(module): change"

PUSH FLOW (AUTOMATED BY KPUSH)
- merges latest main
- blocks on conflict
- commits + pushes safely

CONFLICT RULE
- NEVER rebase
- ALWAYS:

  git merge origin/main

- If conflict:
  KEEP LOCAL STABLE:

  git checkout --ours <file>
  git add .
  git commit -m "merge(main): keep stable local state"

- THEN:
  git push origin feature/<branch>

MERGE
- PR → GitHub merge only
- NO direct pushes to main

POST-MERGE
- git checkout main
- git pull origin main

PROHIBITED
- ❌ git push origin main
- ❌ git push --force main
- ❌ git pull --rebase
- ❌ editing conflicts manually line-by-line
- ❌ multi-module edits
- ❌ mixing UI + runtime + AI changes

AI RULE
- Small targeted edits only
- No full rewrites unless explicitly required
- No architecture changes

ROLLBACK
- Before risky change:

  git tag <module>-checkpoint
  git push origin <module>-checkpoint

- Restore:

  git checkout <tag>

WHAT YOU SHOULD DO NEXT (CURRENT STATE)
You are now safe because:


main is clean and updated


your work is in fix/builder-ui-stable


conflicts already resolved using --ours


Next move (do NOT overthink):
# open PR in GitHub
fix/builder-ui-stable → main
Then:
git checkout main
git pull origin main

CRITICAL INSIGHT (THIS IS WHY THIS MATTERS)
Your builder core is now at the stage where:


preview, fs, ai, builder UI are tightly coupled


a bad merge = silent break (not obvious until runtime)


So:
👉 Git discipline = product stability
Without this guardrail:


you will keep re-breaking “stable” states


you will lose velocity every time



TASK COMPLETE
Files changed


none (this is process enforcement)


Commands to run

fix/builder-ui-stable → main

# 2. After merge
git checkout main
git pull origin main

preview renders → yes


editor visible → yes


filetree populated → yes


save overwrites → yes


diff visible → yes


apply works → yes


no runtime errors → yes
